questions.prompt: A server’s Ethernet interface sends to a second server in the same VLAN through a Layer 2 switch. Both servers have consistent same-subnet addressing. The default gateway is unavailable, but the destination MAC is known. Which outcome is expected if no other faults or policies interfere?

choices.text: Local communication must wait for the gateway to recover
choices.explanation: Same-subnet Layer 2 delivery does not require that gateway.

choices.text: The servers can exchange local traffic through the switch
choices.explanation: The switch can forward between their known local MAC locations.

choices.text: Both servers must use their public addresses
choices.explanation: Local delivery does not require public address assignment.

choices.text: The switch must install a static IP route for the flow
choices.explanation: Ordinary same-VLAN forwarding needs no route for this local flow.

questions.explanation: A default gateway provides a path beyond the directly connected subnet. Local switched traffic can continue without it.

choices.explanation: Ports support transport endpoint identification for both protocols.

choices.explanation: Protocol identity distinguishes the transport namespaces.

choices.explanation: Correct IP connectivity does not make that the direct resolver setting.

choices.text: The DHCP lease duration alone
choices.explanation: Lease duration is not the configured resolver address.

choices.explanation: A VLAN boundary alone is not a prohibition on configured inter-VLAN routing.

choices.text: A switch cannot perform routing under any circumstances.

questions.prompt: Two switches have one link configured as an access port in VLAN 55 at both ends. Each switch has local users only in VLAN 55 for this test. There are no other paths. Can this link extend that one VLAN without being a trunk?

choices.text: Yes; an access link can connect the same single VLAN using untagged frames.
choices.explanation: A trunk is needed for multi-VLAN carriage, not every possible switch-to-switch link.

choices.text: No; the switches need an IP routing adjacency to exchange these same-VLAN frames.
choices.explanation: Layer 2 switching within the VLAN does not require a routing protocol.

choices.text: No; every interswitch cable must be a trunk regardless of the traffic.
choices.explanation: An intentionally configured single-VLAN access link can forward that VLAN.

choices.text: Yes; it automatically carries every VLAN as well.
choices.explanation: An ordinary access link does not provide general multi-VLAN carriage.

questions.explanation: Interface function follows the required traffic scope. A one-VLAN access connection is possible, although trunks are commonly used for multi-VLAN interswitch designs.
